findings.claim: The unsubscribe endpoint is a GET route whose action changes and saves TopicUser.notification_level without CSRF protection or a signed token, so a third-party page (e.g. via ) can change a logged-in user's notification level for any topic they can see.

verifier.reason: config/routes.rb:440-441 exposes topics#unsubscribe as GET routes, and app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:32,98-116 skips check_xhr and directly mutates and saves TopicUser.notification_level without any signed token. Because Rails' protect_from_forgery (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:20) does not verify GET requests, a third-party page can trigger notification-level changes via a cross-site GET such as an tag for a logged-in user.

findings.claim: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, TopicUser.find_by can return nil when the user has no topic_users row for the topic. The next line calls tu.notification_level without a nil check, which raises and returns a 500.

verifier.reason: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105, TopicUser.find_by returns nil when the logged-in user has no topic_users row for the topic (TopicView.new at line 99 does not create one), and app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 immediately calls tu.notification_level without a nil check. Because NoMethodError is not rescued in TopicsController or ApplicationController, this raises an unhandled exception and returns a 500.

findings.claim: TopicsController#unsubscribe calls tu.save! directly instead of TopicUser.change. As a result, notifications_reason_id/notifications_changed_at are not set and the MessageBus notification_level_change publish is skipped, so update_last_read auto-tracking can later overwrite the user's choice.

verifier.reason: TopicsController#unsubscribe (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-116) mutates tu.notification_level and calls tu.save! (line 113) directly instead of TopicUser.change, which leaves notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id unset (app/models/topic_user.rb:87-90) and skips the MessageBus notification_level_change publish (app/models/topic_user.rb:111-113). Because TopicUser.update_last_read auto-tracks whenever tu.notifications_reason_id is null (app/models/topic_user.rb:160-167), subsequent reading can overwrite the user's unsubscribed notification level back to tracking.
